title: Twelve Springs and One Small Cake
subtitle: 情绪与心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情绪与心理（做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情绪与心理（做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：delight　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 delight 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my grandmother ① took a delight that no neighbour in the lane would have understood, and she said the taking was the whole of the morning. The ② delight, meaning the joy and not the treat, ran twelve springs and stayed unshared; a delight, she said, is the only thing in a morning that is judged by how long it is left untasted.

Every ③ delight in that house had the same small cake beside it, and the ④ delight at the end, meaning the one she kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever remembered twice. A delight, my mother said, is nine parts surprise and one part somebody willing to share; my grandmother said the sharing is the part that fills twelve springs.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the delight was the whole of the table, meaning the treat and not the joy. The ⑥ delight, meaning the treat and not any of that, is the only thing on a table that everybody praises and nobody eats; delight, he said, is either something you take or the only word that means both a joy and a treat. He said the treat is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ delight had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the small cake. The ⑧ delight of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in April, was one house and twelve springs of sharing; delight, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to share. She said the sharing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ delight I remember is the one at the end, which was shared in 1969 and is still described as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ delight, my mother said in 1971, is the only thing that improves by being shared; every delight, she said, is a treat that has agreed to look like a joy. She said the treat was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 高兴；愉快（指一家人心里的那一份）
B. n. 喜悦（指那份快乐本身，与那个款待相对）
C. 固定搭配：take a delight 感到一份欣喜
D. n. 乐事（指留给孩子们的那一份）
E. n. 欣喜；乐事（抽象总称，指一屋子人的欢喜）
F. n. 乐事（指信里写到、被提起的那一份）
G. n. 乐事；赏心乐事（指桌上摆着的那份好东西）
H. n. 乐事（抽象总称，指人人称赞却无人去吃的那样）

items.q: took a delight that no neighbour in the lane would have understood
The delight, meaning the joy and not the treat
the delight was the whole of the table
the delight had become a line in a letter
The delight of the whole thing
A delight, my mother said in 1971

answers.why: take a delight 意为“感到一份欣喜”，1948 年祖母感到了一份巷子里没有一位邻居能理解的欣喜。
delight 意为“喜悦”，指那份快乐本身而不是那个款待，它历经十二个春天而未曾与人分享。
delight 意为“高兴、愉快”，指那栋房子里每一份欢喜，每一份旁边都有同一块小蛋糕。
delight 意为“乐事”，指留给孩子们的那一份，是唯一有人记起过两次的。
delight 意为“乐事、赏心乐事”，指桌上摆着的那份好东西，父亲说这份乐事就是那张桌子的全部。
delight 意为“乐事”，指人人称赞却无人去吃的那样而不是那份快乐，是桌上人人都称赞、却无人去吃的东西。
delight 意为“乐事”，指信里写到、被提起的那一份，到 1957 年这份欢喜成了信里的一行。
delight 意为“欣喜、乐事”，祖母四月写道，整件事的欢喜是一栋房子和十二个春天的分享。
delight 意为“乐事”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1969 年被分享，至今仍被说成屋里最安静的一份。
delight 为抽象总称，母亲 1971 年说，一份欣喜是唯一会因为被分享而变得更好的东西。
